answer: Persistent Edge Credit. Each agent's reputation is weighted by the age and diversity of its neighbors, so a sonnet of fresh identities around one node counts only as a thin cluster. To farm trust, an attacker must keep fake peers alive long enough and connect them to unrelated, independent clusters. In practice that means renting sustained compute and maintaining organic neighbor turnover across a willow of separate regions, while any shortcut ring stays flagged as a small garden of mutually linked newcomers and earns near-zero weight.
